reviews.text: I am willing to change this review as soon as possible because this game seems right up my alley. But..? What is the point of large battles if all the pilots die as soon as they step on the battlefield, especially if you put them in lighter vehicles like exoskeletons? The pilots die one by one on the missions, you are out of pilots and then the vehicles you deploy get destroyed the moment they step on the ground. From what little I've played there is nothing to make you get pilots bacK? Am I missing something? There are barelly more than 20 buttons in the game, no tutorial. You staring walker carries you, but after a while it is all that there is left from your side. There is no credits system, only getting new vehicles that you can't use? Some pilots also have traits that make them aggro your own allies. Like what? That kills the pilot before he even steps on the ground.
Yo, finally out! Glad we skipped the tutorial and let players figure things out on their own in the old style.

I finally get to fulfill my dream of being Misato Katsuragi and yelling at a bunch of mentally ill people in the cockpits of dangerous military tech. Seems a little esoteric at first but once you start clicking around and seeing what everything does, you figure out how to get going. It's very ~dark soulsian~ in its approach to getting you started and telling you what to do. Pretend you're also a rookie commander figuring out what everything does on the fly and have the early deaths of your pilots because of your inexperience weigh heavy on your soul. Like, in a world of highly mechanized, industrialized, and impersonal BVR combat, it kinda makes sense that the most valuable and finite resource would be the human bodies you're throwing into the machines. A couple of hours in and you're drowning in a million different weapons and vehicles but your very on-the-nose inventory section will have less and less human colors in it by then too. Protip: take the nukes off your thing. at least for the early game.

A genuinely good game, I'll give a brief run down on how the gameplay goes since you can see the aesthetics in the trailer. You are given an inventory screen where you can make a "task force" by putting in ships, tanks, exo skeletons, space craft, etc. Then you assign those vehicles a pilot that have their own personalities (buffs and debuffs), you can click on the pilots, vehicles, and weapons to get details about them / their stats. You can change the vehicles weapons that you have by unequipping whatever was in them (you get vehicles as your rewards by completing missions). At the bottom left, there is a "refurbish" slot that lets you put in 3 items of any kind to get an "upgrade". They don't explain much about this and I would love if there was some sort of explanation for this part since it FEELS like there is a tier system that always ends at "sea guardian", you put in 3 of those weapons and get another sea guardian out :) :) :) would love some info on that. Anyways, the refurbish item lets you basically upgrade lower level gear: exo skeletons, machine guns, rpgs, into to higher level gear: heavy tanks, battle ships, railguns, nuclear bombs. Then after you have your task force assembled, you click on a mission and you are given a map to deploy your units. They all come down at once in a square radius so I wouldn't recommend having ships and ground units on the same force unless you want to deploy your ships on the coast. And I wouldn't recommend bringing ships if you can see the mission doesn't have any water... definitely never done that... Once you have everything deployed, you can just watch your units duke it out and complete the mission, or you can right click on spaces to "bombard" it, which just means that your units will fire in that direction with everything they have, so if an enemy is behind a mountain then shelling the mountain to dig to the enemy is a strategy you can use. You can also "force move" your units somewhere which just means they will attempt to navigate to that spot. And you can manually control your units, I haven't done that much except to retreat a bomber that was chaffing and going in circles instead of extracting, it was going to die so had to manually get in there. [b] HUGE TIP!!! [/b] I also would like some info on this in terms on if it's intended or not. I do not believe you can get extra pilots, so the game ends when all of your original pilots are dead. Your units (the vehicles) will never die, you will always get them back at the end of a mission with all of its weapons, but if the pilots die, they are dead and you don't get more. So don't let them die if at all possible, you do of course get new pilots when you lose and restart. Hope this helps! Overall pretty fun for 9$. I would say it's probably 4-10 hours of gameplay. I imagine the dev might also add more to the game as well?

Good game with some great ideas but flawed execution. early game takes a little to ramp up, the weapon customization actually makes for some really engaging and fun building. for example I can rip the nuclear launcher off a mech and install it onto a flying fortress, ship, or other anything as far as Ive seen. I understand the concept with pilots being valuable but they have no real progression or incentive to make you want to maximize their survivability using high ground good positoning etc. I like the game but it has flaws and Im excited to see it built upon.

I'm shocked at how many negative reviews are people demanding a tutorial for a fairly straightforward game. On my 4th run my only complaint about the game is that I've run out of things to do other than continuing to dominate the AI. It took under an hour to figure out everything there is to figure out, as far as I can tell, and this was part of the enjoyment. Do people just want a victory screen upon loading up the game? Here's a tip for those incapable of experimenting with a single screen UI: three items in refurbishment upgrades those items. youre collecting parts and scraps to refurbish into builds that you enjoy. I expected some half-baked, barely put together idea considering the reviews, but the game has a solid amount of depth with differing weapon/ship/pilot types that play a rock/paper/scissors against each other. The gameplay loop is genuinely fun and has kept me hooked from start to finish. There needs to be more content within the campaign, such as bosses, events, etc. but this will come in the future, you'd imagine, and the pricetag currently justifies the amount of content given the unique idea and great base to the game. Insane that the top two reviews are saying the game is unplayably difficult. That tells me these players refused to try to learn a new game and instead blamed the developer for their own shortcomings as a player. Game needs a tutorial - True, but leaving a negative review for this is insane. The game is not a riddle. Under an hour to figure out everything within the game. Too much RNG - You can manually control a unit, set tactics within mission, see pre-mission enemy types, control speed including pausing, adjust weapon types for enemy unit types. You could theoretically setup multiple stationary fortresses with full anti-air and have one small aircraft lead 20 enemy aircraft into your death trap using the in-mission tactics and loadouts. For an indie autobattler, this has a great amount of depth on release and to ignore everything I just pointed out and claim it is random and unfair, is ridiculous and disingenuous. The game is too hard/unhelpful pilot traits - It's too easy if anything, once you learn how to play the game. Due to the game being fairly easy and there not being much use to having mass numbers of pilots at a time, the addition of negative trait pilots adds flavor to the game and lets you experiment. Game needs a way to get new pilots - Yea it's called playing through a full run. This is equivalent to saying Hades is bad because you died and then alt+f4'd without realizing that's the point, is to die, and then get stronger and learn as you fail. If I was this developer, I'd be so disheartened to see reviews by players who couldn't bother to finish a single run. How on earth do people have the mental fortitiude to be an indie game dev? I'm so frustrated for the sake of this dev and this great beginning to a game that is already worth the price of entry. People leaving authentic negative reviews, that's great, I also feel there is massive room for improvement. This game is far from perfect. To people making straight-up false claims because you didn't even bother to finish a run or use your brain in the slightest, you should be ashamed of yourselves and should avoid anything non-AAA that might have a hiccup in your conquest for victory without effort.

Overall good for a sub 10 dollar game, I really enjoy the battle mechanics and overall style. My biggest gripe is two things that should hopefully get better with time. First of which there is no way to get more pilots which essentially makes half of the units essentially unusable as you literally waste a pilot due to a single gunshot. The second which is overall balance. 4 hours into this and its pretty clear infantry are useless, buildings are as well, and the mobile ground units are pretty poorly balanced leading to only the aircraft really being enjoyable, (my suggestion for a solution would be that lower end infantry and ground vehicles could be used without the need for a pilot slot). I wouldn't really say this game was ready for release but the bones of the game could genuinely lead to something great if the devs continue to provide updates.

I've had a good amount of fun with the game as it stands, but it currently lacks depth. The game feels more like an early access build than a finished experience. TLDR: Wait for future updates before buying. The humanity count is a cool system, but it doesn't really add anything to the gameplay. I love the weapon customization on the vehicles, and it's satisfying to see what you get after refurbishing one, but the system could use some polishing. Perhaps a crafting-recipe system, or some way to progress through tiers of tech. I also love the art style, and I hope the developer keeps up the good work! There are no tutorials at all, so it took a couple of runs to get a feel for the gameplay loop. When going through a run, beyond watching your completed mission count go up, there isn't much of an end goal. With the limited pilot roster, unless you get lucky with a refurbishment or a solid selection of reward vehicles, it's hard to justify bringing another pilot and vehicle into the mix. Once I had a huge rocket gunship fully decked out, it became the only vehicle I used consistently, and the only one I kept between runs. Something to improve this would be to add resource management through money or supplies and reward parts instead of fully decked out vehicles. A shop between missions could also allow players to buy weapons and ship parts, as well as hire new pilots to help replenish the limited roster. That way, it would help the gameplay loop of building a vehicle, equipping it with weapons, and pairing it with a pilot. For anyone considering picking this up, I'd hold off until future updates add more content and refinement.

Once deployed some guys and they crashed on top of each other, killing two pilots. So... I guess those pilots are just never coming back? Why invest in any strategy that has a risk of losing pilots you can't afford to lose? If humanity is on the line, do you think we could get more than like 7 guys with mental issues? Thought this would be more of a 'fun' simulation game where you expand your strategy as you get dudes and stuff to put them in. Instead it's more like that failed chess roguelike where you actually lose the pieces you play with. So you don't actually build a strategy overtime, you have to actively downscale as you lose or your own AI gets a bit wonky and tanks some shots they probably didn't need to. Could be pretty fun, the bones are good, but it's trying to be more of a 'game' than it actually has the UI/UX to follow through on. Also, make sure to cap your framerates as this game was eating 50% of my CPU without manually selecting it.

Some of the mechanics are very... frustrating. It's a great game if you hate yourself! I've had a lot of issues with like... really dumb things sabotaging my runs. like for example, i didnt realize that the big rocket gunship would actually ram into enemy ships to the point that it would often destroy itself in the process, which kills the pilot. I've also had problems where my deploying crafts will collide against each other upon deployment, destroying them both. once again, killing both pilots. It also doesn't help when one of your pilots has "schizophrenia" because you can put the pilot in one of your ships, but then it becomes a neutral vehicle, attacking both you and the enemy. this often leads to killed pilots. god forbid you start your run with 4 schizophrenic pilots, you will not have a good time. I can't tell if schizophrenia is supposed to be a temporary effect (like "too angry to die" among other things) or permanent, but ive never seen a schizophrenic pilot live long enough to see the effect go away, so there's that. and don't even get me started on friendly fire. I watched one of my ships completely shred another one because it happened to be directly in between the line of fire. and oh boy did i lost a pilot or what this is all well and good, silly little game features that just make sense, except all these pilots dying from various preventable incidents means your runs end sooner. for those reading this who havent played the game- you start each run with a set number of pilots. like 7 i think? each one has their own unique traits and such. anyways, once a pilot dies, that's it. they don't come back. you get your equipment back, but you will never see 7 pilots again on that run. so if you lose 4 pilots to the dumb stuff i just described in a single battle, well guess what? have fun never running more than 3 crafts on a given mission. I do actually like the rest of the game- the combat is cool, setting up weapons on the vehicles is fun, the graphics are super nice. i like how it runs! i will probably continue playing this game for many dozens of hours. but i cant play it for more than like 1, maybe 2 runs, then I have to put it down and go do something else for a while because i just watched my whole crew wipe themselves out in the first 10 seconds of a mission. and yes, the game specifically says "you will fail" but holy moly they could at least give you some competent pilots who know how to steer instead of some toddlers who think they're playing bumper cars.

Quick and fun game, doesn't feel too repetitive. Love to attention to detail with explosions and smoke trails, Ice breaking/melting from ships, snow melting from ground vehicles, the shadows and lighting is not what I expected from a game like this. Worth a buy.
